reader.summary: Turkey made several major diplomatic moves this week. Canadian PM Mark Carney visited Ankara and the two countries signed a strategic partnership covering trade, defense, and energy; Carney also raised LGBTQ+ rights issues and named AtkinsRealis as a contender for a Turkish nuclear plant. Separately, Turkey, Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, Qatar, and Indonesia signed a defense cooperation accord, the Mecca Pact, under which Turkey plans to send military personnel to Saudi Arabia, and the treaty was submitted to the Turkish parliament for ratification. On the economic front, Turkey cut its interest rate for the first time since the Iran War began, even as the 18-billion-dollar investment fund crisis deepened: the market regulator chief stepped down, three brokerage firms were shut, JPMorgan's Turkey securities unit said it would cease operations, and a fund liquidation law was passed. The Turkey-Libya maritime deal was approved by Eastern Libya's parliament, drawing sharp rejection from Greece and Egypt, with a US senator calling Turkey's behavior thuggish. Istanbul experienced its worst floods in 80 years, killing four people. Police raided the pro-opposition Halk TV channel. Turkey also hosted eight countries in Istanbul for peace talks on regional conflicts.

display.eli5:
Turkey signed a big defense deal with Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, Qatar, and Indonesia. Now the deal goes to parliament for a vote, and opposition parties want to make sure the government does not commit too many soldiers to foreign wars. This is the biggest political story of the week.

The money markets are in trouble. A big investment fund scandal caused the regulator to quit, a major bank to leave the country, and a new law to be passed that will start returning people's money. Next week a new regulator will be named and the first payouts will begin.

Greece is angry about a sea-border deal Turkey made with Libya. It will probably file a formal legal complaint, and Turkey will respond with a sharp diplomatic note, making the Aegean dispute even more heated.

A surprise would be the peace talks Turkey hosted in Istanbul actually producing a written proposal about Iran, making Turkey a bigger player in the region than most people expect.

history_used.HISTORY_BULLETINS:
Round 2026-10-17:
This week in Turkey was dominated by a sharp escalation in the government's control over media. On a reported Thursday, police raided the headquarters of Halk TV, one of the country's last major opposition-aligned broadcasters, halted its live broadcasts, and the state moved to place the channel under a government-appointed trustee. Press freedom groups warned the seizure signaled a broader crackdown, and the move drew international attention. Simultaneously, Istanbul endured its heaviest rainfall in roughly 80 to 84 years, with flooding that killed at least three people, forced school closures, and left streets of damaged vehicles. On the economic front, MSCI froze changes to Turkey equity indexes amid a stock-fixing scandal and fund turmoil, sending Turkish stocks down more than three percent in a single session and raising the specter of a downgrade. The government also let the lira slide faster than previously expected to avoid a sudden future devaluation.
- Halk TV government takeover (dominant, escalating): Police raided Halk TV's Istanbul headquarters, halted live broadcasts, and the state appointed a trustee to run the channel, drawing warnings of a broader opposition-media crackdown.
- Istanbul record flooding (dominant, new): Heaviest rainfall in roughly 80 to 84 years flooded Istanbul, killing at least three people, closing schools, and leaving streets of damaged vehicles.
- MSCI index freeze and stock-fixing scandal (dominant, escalating): MSCI froze changes to Turkey equity indexes amid a stock-fixing scandal and fund turmoil, sending Turkish stocks down over three percent and raising the risk of a market downgrade.
- Erdogan 2028 election float (regular, new): Ankara suggested moving the next general election to 2028, which would reset the term clock and allow President Erdogan to seek another term.
- Lira managed devaluation (regular, continuing): The government accelerated the lira's scheduled depreciation to avoid the risk of a sharp one-off devaluation later.
- US-Turkey diplomatic friction (regular, new): A US senator accused Turkey of thuggish behavior toward Greece and Cyprus, adding a transatlantic dimension to Turkey's Aegean disputes.
- Akkuyu nuclear timeline (occasional, continuing): Rosatom confirmed it is targeting a year-end start-up for Turkey's Akkuyu nuclear plant, the first nuclear power station built in the country.
- Headscarf ban and Azerbaijan row (occasional, new): A school headscarf ban in Azerbaijan triggered rare protests and a diplomatic spat with Turkey, a traditional supporter of Azerbaijan.
- Oldest shipwreck discovery (occasional, new): Researchers announced the discovery of the world's oldest known shipwreck off the Turkish coast, a significant archaeological find.
- Made in Europe plan (occasional, new): A Turkish minister urged the EU not to exclude Turkey from its 'Made in Europe' industrial plan, signaling Ankara's desire for closer economic alignment.
